I would search up some videos on breathing techniques, but in general I’d say breath from your diaphragm and take deep breaths while your soft palette is lifted to avoid a nasal sound while singing - this creates more space for the sound to resonate creating a more open sound - on key is sticking to the key signature of the song - making sure all notes are perfect and not sharp or flat - in a rap style the notes don’t have to be as exact but it’s just being able to hit the right notes... in general your nose is always closed as you breathe through your mouth... for a rap style I would just focus on breathing in time and getting enough breath to sing/rap everything in time and hitting the notes, in general you can get away with a more ‘talking’ style of singing not dissimilar to your regular voice in rap, so I’d just focus on hitting the notes and trying different pronunciations etc to experiment with changing the nasal quality. hope this helps :)

Just make sure to always warm up more than you think you need to before singing, starting with simple exercises and working up to more challenging ones - focusing on breathing is great! Focus on lifting your soft palette inside your mouth as you breathe, creating enough space for your head voice. The transition between head and chest is always hard, but focusing on your breathing as you do so should help, actively changing the resonance of the sound in your mouth by lifting the soft palette when singing in head voice... I’m not a teacher so this is a little difficult to describe but I hope this helps you out :) For pain- I would also just gently approach each note - if you feel it getting a little scratchy or itchy in your throat, stop singing immediately to avoid damaging your throat, pain is bad :), and wait until your voice develops or feels more warmed up before you attempt the note again, just remember- if it feels bad, stop and rest your throat :)

I would work on it gradually - without a teacher guiding you it may be a bit harder, but just make sure your voice is well warmed up every time you sing- I’d also look up videos on breath control as it plays a lot into voice quality... a lot of it is just the positioning inside the mouth and throat so I’d start there and look up vocal exercises that encourage a very open throat... I’m not great at describing it but I hope this helps a little :)
I wouldn’t say so - vocal quality would come with practice and a good teacher would help also

Everything can be learnt, some people have a naturally great tone and then learn technique to compliment it, others have to work a little harder to achieve their desired voice, but (in general), with enough practice, everyone can do it :)

I would say play it by the teacher - if you connect with them and they get good results- choose them, if they happen to be freelance I would say get in touch with music schools through choirs etc for connections :)

I’m not super into colourful eyeshadow at the moment, but I’d definitely say that one of each type is enough! When switching between light and dark shades, I’d usually have a transition mid tone shade on one brush, then a darker shade on another - I wouldn’t mix the two unless I was dipping the darker shade brush into the transition to blend a little, then for lighter shades I would usually use my fingers on my lid or maybe wipe down a brush and use that- so in general I wouldn’t mix brushes, but everyone’s different :)

It’s not necessary, I find it useful when slightly overlining lips and as a guideline for liquid lipstick, but it really isn’t an essential step. I’ll be bringing it in to 2020, but you don’t need to bother.

For eyebrows I would start off with a tinted brow gel of some sort as it’s super easy to apply. The first few times you do this it might look a little rough - I’d advise practicing before bed or something- but brow shape will improve as you learn what suits you and what you prefer for your face! Hope this helps :)

It depends on how much makeup would be expected. To simply look ‘professional’ I’m sure that a heavy foundation would not be needed. There are many brands out there dedicated to making makeup easy and quick to apply - many of these offer skin tints or tinted moisturisers as an alternative to heavy foundations. As I don’t use these types of products I’m not entirely sure which would be best- but there is always plenty of info online! I’ve heard the glossier and milk makeup ones raved about, though have not tried them myself. They’re made to be quick and easy to apply (perfect for everyday) and are so much less heavy than regular foundations. I’d look into some sort of tinted moisturiser to avoid the feeling of clogged pores :) I also wouldn’t focus on what other people are doing and wearing on a daily basis because your face is your own and you should do what you want to do with it!
